left.name: electrical engineering
left.definition: Electrical systems, substations, variable speed drives, analyzers and power supply for CCUS facilities.

right.name: electrical engineering
right.definition: A discipline addressing the design and application of circuitry and equipment for power generation and distribution

left.name: environmental
left.definition: Environmental monitoring, permitting, impact assessment and regulatory reporting.

right.name: environmental
right.definition: A discipline addressing the interface between capital project and the natural environment, specifically addressing risk analysis and mitigation to impact to air, water, flora and fauna.

left.name: environmental
left.definition: Environmental monitoring, permitting, impact assessment and regulatory reporting.

right.name: Environmental

left.name: filter
left.definition: A separator intended to remove solids from vapour or liquid.

left.name: health, safety, environmental and security
left.definition: CO2 release, dispersion, emergency response, environmental monitoring and HSE deliverables.

right.name: health, safety, environmental and security
right.definition: A macro discipline used to classify content generally addressing a combination of 'safety', 'security', 'health' and 'environmental', or any combination thereof.

left.name: information management
left.definition: CCUS data governance, MRV data, RDL governance and digital handover.

right.name: information management
right.definition: A discipline addressing the collection and management of information both in document and data formats

left.name: instrumentation engineering
left.definition: CO2 analyzers, flow metering, pressure monitoring, leak detection, SCADA and control systems.

right.name: instrumentation engineering
right.definition: A discipline addressing the design and application of monitoring and control systems.

left.name: maintenance management
left.definition: Inspection, integrity, maintenance, spare parts and monitoring programs.

right.name: maintenance management
right.definition: A discipline addressing equipment reliability and planning required to maintain the equipment and other infrastructure. Includes procedures, spares, etc.

left.name: maintenance strategy
left.definition: A document outlining purpose and approach for maintenance in case of preventive, breakdown or shutdown maintenance.

right.name: maintenance strategy
right.definition: Maintenance, spares, membrane replacement and asset health strategy.

left.name: materials engineering
left.definition: CO2 corrosion, materials compatibility, solvent degradation and pipeline materials.

right.name: materials engineering
right.definition: A discipline addressing material selection and methods to manage integrity for the facility lifecycle, including corrosion management through coatings, linings, cathodic protection, inhibition, weld procedures, etc.

left.name: mechanical engineering
left.definition: Cross-mechanical CCUS package equipment.

right.name: mechanical engineering
right.definition: A macro discipline used to classify content generally addressing a combination of 'piping', HVAC, 'rotating', or 'static equipment', or any combination thereof.

left.name: mechanical rotating engineering
left.definition: CO2 compression, pumps and rotating equipment.

right.name: mechanical rotating engineering
right.definition: A mechanical engineering specialty addressing mechanical components used to add kinetic energy to any process in order to make a material move. The equipment may include pumps, turbines, gearboxes, compressors, engines, etc.

left.name: mechanical static engineering
left.definition: Columns, tanks, vessels, dehydration packages and terminals.

right.name: mechanical static engineering
right.definition: A mechanical engineering specialty addressing mechanical equipment with no rotating components.  The equipment may include tanks, vessels, heat exchangers, and fired equipment such as furnaces and boilers.

left.name: metal
left.definition: Are flat and vertical, which are constructed using a frame and metal boards, used for separation.

right.name: milligram per litre
right.definition: TDS, boron, residuals and other concentrations.

left.name: operations handover
left.definition: Final operational, monitoring, permit and MRV information required for operations handover.

right.name: operations handover
right.definition: Final operations, maintenance, water quality and asset data accepted.

left.name: operations management
left.definition: Operating procedures, injection operations, transport operations and site handover.

right.name: operations management
right.definition: A discipline related to the planning, scheduling and future operations management post turnover. Including but not limited to training materials, procedures, strategies, organization design, etc.

left.name: pipeline engineering
left.definition: CO2 pipeline transportation systems, pipeline integrity, route, block valves and vent stations.

right.name: pipeline engineering
right.definition: A discipline addressing the systems that are used to transport liquids and gases. Including but not limited to pipeline design hydraulics, routes & stability,specification and other accessories such as cathodic protection, pigging equipment etc.

left.name: piping engineering
left.definition: CO2 process piping, solvent piping, valves, materials and flow assurance.

right.name: piping engineering
right.definition: A mechanical engineering specialty addressing the design, routing, and control of flow inside process and utilities via piping and related specialty equipment

left.name: pressure
left.definition: Force perpendicular to the area divided by area. p = dF/dA where dF is the  perpendicular component of the force acting on the area element dA. The pressure is positive when the force is acting into the area.

left.name: process engineering
left.definition: Capture process design, CO2 conditioning, mass balance and flow assurance.

right.name: process engineering
right.definition: A discipline related to the design, operation, control, and optimization of chemical, physical, and biological processes. Including but not limited to process flow definition, process modeling, etc.

left.name: process flow diagram
left.definition: A diagram detailing major items of equipment, primary lines and valves, operating temperatures, pressures and mass flows. Diagrams shall be provided for all hydrocarbon and utilities systems. Includes 'utility flow schemes/diagrams' [UFS/UFD].

right.name: process flow diagram
right.definition: Process flow diagram for treatment/desalination systems.

left.name: pump
left.definition: A physical object that adds or removes mechanical energy to a fluid, either constantly or periodically.

left.name: tank
left.definition: A vessel intended to contain fluid for storage. Typically a receiving or collecting function for further distribution. Typically with a vertical and cylindrical or square shape and a flat or conical bottom.

left.name: temperature
left.definition: The degree or intensity of heat or cold as measured on a thermometric scale, and a measure of whether two systems are relatively hot or cold with respect to one another. Two systems brought into contact will, after sufficient time, be in thermal equilibrium and will have the same temperature.
